title: A candidate that must earn its place
subtitle: BUB1B-MVA · arimoclomol · functional rescue
label: 01 / THE QUESTION
narration: For a child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy, a plausible medicine is only a starting point. We propose arimoclomol for laboratory testing, with explicit rules for deciding whether it deserves to advance. We have not demonstrated drug rescue or treated this child. Our contribution is a testable proposal, supported by working tools that others can use.
bullets: Question: can functional BubR1 be restored?
Status: proposed experiment; no drug rescue yet

title: Measure the variant before choosing its remedy
subtitle: Protein amount and protein function are different questions
label: 02 / THE MECHANISM
narration: The two identified variants affect the gene that makes Bub R one, a protein involved in chromosome separation. Their phase is inferred. The exact protein consequences remain unmeasured. The missense variant could reduce abundance, impair function, do both, or remain indeterminate. We compare full-length normal and altered protein at matched abundance. An isolated fragment's melting curve cannot settle that question.
bullets: Full-length WT and N1002K, abundance matched

title: Three gates between a molecule and a claim
subtitle: Exposure → response → chromosome-segregation function
label: 03 / THE EXPERIMENT
narration: Arimoclomol has a human approval in a different disease. Its reported effects depend on the cell and the stress. That makes exposure a gate, not a footnote. First, qualify the model and measurement. Second, test whether the proposed response occurs at relevant exposure. Third, require better chromosome segregation, while tracking division, survival and cell fate. More protein alone does not pass. Neither does an apparent improvement caused by stopping division or selectively losing abnormal cells. Failed controls are indeterminate; a valid drug negative stops that tested approach.
bullets: Exclude cytostasis, death and selection as explanations

title: A gene name should lead to evidence
subtitle: An offline navigator with uncertainty kept visible
label: 04 / THE REUSABLE TOOL
narration: We also built a practical gene-to-condition navigator. Search a gene, inspect its candidate condition mappings, and follow the source evidence. It includes every row of a dated, two thousand and sixty-three row register snapshot, including thirty-five unmapped rows and source disagreements. A match is not an eligibility decision, and no match is not evidence of ineligibility. Queries stay on the device.
bullets: A lookup aid, not an eligibility decision

title: An empty result must never pass
subtitle: Portable checks for the interpretation layer
label: 05 / THE RIGOR
narration: Our interpretation canary checks that a model has actually answered. Real Splice A I inference passes six controls. A separate checker self-test rejects nine injected failures, including missing and nonfinite output. We distinguish those tests from clinical accuracy. A public-genome spike-in also demonstrates scale, while leaving diagnostic performance and knowledge leakage unresolved.
bullets: 6 controls passed with real model inference
9 injected failures rejected by the checker
Missing prerequisites return NOT RUN, never success
source: Measured SpliceAI output 2026-10-23 · public HG002 smoke test

title: The next result is clear
subtitle: Does N1002K retain function that this candidate can rescue?
label: 06 / THE NEXT STEP
narration: The next step is a laboratory test of full-length variant function and exposure-limited rescue. The proposal says what would advance the candidate and what would stop it. The reusable tools, source trail and plain-language explanation are delivered now. Clinical benefit remains to be earned. That is the standard we want this work judged against.
bullets: Delivered: code, source trail, protocol, communication
Next: independent functional and exposure validation
No claim of a proven treatment
